A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ParaUni study, with readable text, equations, algorithms, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. Both end with references; neither includes an appendix or the supplementary material repeatedly cited in Sections 3–4. These assessments cover all supplied pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original ParaUni benchmark results, component ablations, layer analyses and reward-training curves, including Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–5 and 9.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for applying ParaUni to Janus-Pro and BLIP-3o in Table 4.

M1.justification: The LIM, LDAM, frozen VLM, three training stages, Equations 4–6 and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Table 4 reports applications to other models but describes no new component or procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: The named training corpora and GenEval/DPG-Bench tasks remain unchanged. Table 4 varies the underlying models rather than dataset or task coverage. Changed dataset citations do not establish that different training data were used.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their comparator membership. New Table 4 adds paired comparisons of Janus-Pro (1B) and BLIP-3o (4B) against their ParaUni-equipped versions; these models appeared previously, but these controlled comparisons did not.

E3.justification: Table 4 introduces additional model configurations and with/without-ParaUni controls on the existing benchmarks. Settings for the original experiments remain unchanged. Integration-specific training budgets, preprocessing and evaluation procedures for the new comparisons are not disclosed.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 adds an applicability analysis testing whether ParaUni benefits two other baseline models. The existing layer-selection, LIM and LDAM ablations in Table 3, together with the layer/reward analyses, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies explicit seed counts, repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained reward curves use the same presentation, and Table 4 introduces no additional uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical values, including ParaUni's 0.87 GenEval and 83.45 DPG-Bench scores. New Table 4 reports Janus-Pro without/with ParaUni at 0.73/0.80 and 82.63/83.65, and BLIP-3o at 0.81/0.84 and 79.36/81.97. These are newly reported comparisons, not performance improvements between versions. v1's six-image sample gallery is removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and their mathematical content are unchanged. No new formal assumption, definition, derivation, theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical conditioning, LIM, LDAM and state-of-the-art generation. The additional experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: The new Section 4.5 paragraph interprets Table 4 as evidence that ParaUni is a general, plug-and-play module effective on other, weaker baselines. Existing mechanism explanations and result interpretations remain unchanged, with no new substantive limitations.

D1.justification: v2 removes the direct text-to-image-2M and Megalith-10M dataset access references, including the latter's caption-variant information; the retained dataset names now cite TextAtlas5M and Public Domain 12M. It adds computational-provenance acknowledgments for the MCC GPU cluster and AI-Scientist platform. Existing hyperparameters and the code URL are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds STAGE, MaskFocus and group critical-token policy optimization citations, removes InstructBLIP and the original BLIP3-o reference, and substitutes dataset references. Retained BLIP3-o mentions now cite BLIP3o-next. The main positioning relative to earlier multilayer-conditioning approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammar, punctuation and citation-formatting edits, adds a technique-contributor footnote and acknowledgments, and inserts the short other-baselines paragraph. The section sequence and overall narrative remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 4 and removes v1 Figure 8's six-image gallery. The retained reward curves and qualitative comparison become Figures 8 and 9, respectively. Figures and tables are resized or repositioned within the existing two-column layout, without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Table 4 adds potentially useful evidence of applicability beyond the original backbone, and copyediting modestly improves readability. However, the new integrations lack implementation and training details, while changed references create dataset and baseline provenance mismatches. The limited documentation makes the value of the added evidence difficult to weigh against the loss of traceability, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
